testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What is a tank endorsement?

options.text: Needed when transporting liquids and gases.

questions.correctAnswerText: Needed when transporting liquids and gases.
questions.explanation: You need a tank endorsement to drive a tank vehicle that carries liquids or gases. This applies to both hazardous and non-hazardous materials.

questions.question: When you push the brake pedal, how do air brakes respond?

options.text: Only if it is warm outside.

questions.correctAnswerText: After a short delay.
questions.explanation: Air brakes have a delay because air needs time to travel through the brake lines. Usually there is at least half a second between when you press the brake pedal and when the brakes start to work.

questions.question: When must you sign a written vehicle inspection report?

options.text: Only if defects were found and repaired.
Only if repairs cost more than $1,000.
Only if a police officer asks you to.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only if defects were found and repaired.
questions.explanation: You must sign the inspection report only if defects were found and certified as repaired or not needing repair.

questions.question: What should you do if a vehicle is tailgating you?
questions.correctAnswerText: Drive in the right lane.
questions.explanation: If your heavy load is slowing you down, stay in the right lane when possible to let faster traffic pass.

questions.question: How much water on the road can cause hydroplaning?
questions.correctAnswerText: Just a small amount.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires lose grip on the road and slide on a layer of water. You do not need much water for this to happen.

questions.question: What is the best way to avoid cell phone distractions while driving?

options.text: Stay on one call for the entire trip.
Turn the phone off before driving.
Only use the phone for incoming calls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the phone off before driving.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid cell phone distractions is to turn off your phone before you start driving and keep it off until you reach your destination.

questions.question: What should you do before driving downhill?

options.text: Use only the brakes to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift into a lower gear.
questions.explanation: On a steep downhill, use the engine to help control your speed. Shift to a lower gear before going downhill. Using only brakes can cause them to overheat and fail.

questions.question: What should you do with your cell phone when driving in heavy traffic?

options.text: Do not use your phone at all.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use your phone at all.
questions.explanation: Heavy traffic, construction, pedestrians, and bad weather require your full attention. You should avoid all distractions, including cell phone use, in these conditions.

questions.question: During an air brake leakage test, what is the maximum amount of pressure loss allowed in one minute?
questions.correctAnswerText: 2 psi
questions.explanation: The maximum leakage allowed in an air brake system is 2 psi per minute. If air leaks faster than this, the vehicle should not be driven and repairs are needed.

questions.question: What danger occurs if your vehicle rolls backward when you start to accelerate?

options.text: You may hit a vehicle behind you.
You may lose your place in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may hit a vehicle behind you.
questions.explanation: To avoid hitting a vehicle or object behind you, make sure your vehicle does not roll backward when starting from a stop. If you have a manual transmission, partly engage the clutch before releasing the brake.

questions.question: When stopped on the side of the road, a driver should:

options.text: Keep the driver's side door open.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on emergency flashers.
questions.explanation: When you stop on the side of the road, turn on your emergency flashers to warn other drivers. This is especially important at night.

questions.question: When inspecting cargo, the driver should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Make sure the truck is not overloaded.
Make sure the cargo is balanced.
Make sure the cargo is secured properly.
Place breakable items under heavier items.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place breakable items under heavier items.
questions.explanation: Drivers should inspect cargo to make sure it is properly secured, balanced, and not over the weight limit. Breakable items should not be placed under heavier items.

questions.question: A modulating control valve can control the:
questions.correctAnswerText: Spring brakes.
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve lets a driver gradually apply spring brakes. In equipped vehicles, a lever on the dashboard controls the valve.

questions.question: If you feel tired and yawn frequently, you should:

options.text: Pull over and take a nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and take a nap.
questions.explanation: Frequent yawning means you are tired. The only safe thing to do is stop and sleep. Coffee will not keep you alert long enough and will make you more tired later.

questions.question: After you start the engine, oil pressure should reach normal level:
questions.correctAnswerText: Within a few seconds.
questions.explanation: After you start the engine, watch the gauges. Oil pressure should reach normal level within a few seconds.

questions.question: Regarding winter driving, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: Front tires need a tread depth of at least 4/32 of an inch.
Rear tires need a tread depth of at least 2/32 of an inch.
Use a gauge to check that each tire has safe tread depth.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tires should be slightly deflated.
questions.explanation: In winter, your tires need good tread. Front tires need at least 4/32 of an inch tread, and rear tires need at least 2/32 of an inch. Check tread depth with a gauge. Never deflate tires.

questions.question: What is a Gross Vehicle Weight Rating?

options.text: The maximum weight that the manufacturer says a loaded vehicle can weigh.
The maximum weight that can be pulled by a vehicle.
The minimum weight that can be hauled by a vehicle.
The maximum amount that can be loaded on a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum weight that the manufacturer says a loaded vehicle can weigh.
questions.explanation: Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) is the maximum weight that the manufacturer says a vehicle and its cargo can weigh.

questions.question: You should always be able to stop within:

options.text: The distance you can see ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The distance you can see ahead.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle must be able to stop within the distance you can see. Slow down when visibility is poor.

questions.question: If a truck is equipped with one, a trailer brake hand valve can be used to:

options.text: Stop the vehicle from rolling back when starting from a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the vehicle from rolling back when starting from a stop.
questions.explanation: A trailer brake hand valve stops a tractor-trailer from rolling back when starting from a stop.

questions.question: Vehicles with dual air brake systems:

options.text: Have air pressure in the brakes even when the engine is off.
Keep some air pressure in the brakes when the engine is off.
Must run to build air pressure before the brakes can work.
Keep air pressure when shut off for less than four hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must run to build air pressure before the brakes can work.
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, let the engine run so the compressor builds air pressure of at least 100 psi in both systems.

questions.question: What do air tank drains do?

options.text: They allow rain water to enter the tanks.
They remove water and oil from the air tanks.
They must stay open while you are driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: They remove water and oil from the air tanks.
questions.explanation: Compressed air in an air brake system contains water and compressor oil. Water and oil can damage the brakes if they build up in the system. Open the air tank drains each day to remove this buildup.

questions.question: What might you be asked to do on a basic vehicle control skills test?

options.text: Pull forward into a parking space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parallel park.
questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test may include straight line backing, offset back/right parking, offset back/left parking, driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT an effect of drinking alcohol and then driving?
questions.correctAnswerText: Faster reaction time
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time. Drinking and driving can cause you to straddle lanes, start abruptly, forget to signal, run stop signs and red lights, and pass incorrectly. Alcohol makes your reactions slower, not faster.

questions.question: What is an encroachment on a basic vehicle control skills test?

options.text: Putting the vehicle in neutral and using the parking brake.
The vehicle touching an exercise boundary line.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle touching an exercise boundary line.
questions.explanation: An encroachment happens when any part of your vehicle touches or crosses an exercise boundary line. Each encroachment counts as an error.

questions.question: What helps you know when to shift to a higher gear?
questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above
questions.explanation: Two things tell you when to shift up. First is engine speed (rpm). Check your vehicle's manual to learn the right rpm range and shift up when you reach the top. Second is road speed (mph). Learn which speeds work for each gear, then watch your speedometer and shift up as needed.

questions.question: What should be true about the leaves on a leaf spring?
questions.correctAnswerText: They should not be broken.
questions.explanation: Check leaf springs for broken or missing leaves. Any broken leaves are dangerous. If one-fourth or more of the leaves are missing from any leaf spring, the vehicle cannot be driven.

questions.question: What should engine belts be like?
questions.correctAnswerText: Tight.
questions.explanation: Check engine belts to make sure they are tight and not worn. The right amount of tightness varies by engine, so check your vehicle's needs.

questions.question: With low beam headlights on, you should see about ____ ahead of your vehicle.
questions.correctAnswerText: 250 feet
questions.explanation: Low beam headlights let you see about 250 feet ahead. When driving at night, slow down so you can stop within the distance your headlights show.

questions.question: Is texting while driving a commercial motor vehicle allowed?

options.text: Yes, if the text is work-related.
Yes, if the message has fewer than 10 words.
Yes, because it is safer than talking on the phone.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, it is prohibited.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving a commercial motor vehicle is illegal and dangerous. Typing text into or reading text from any device is considered texting.

questions.question: Where should your vehicle's final position be?

options.text: Exactly where the examiner told you.
Within five feet of where the examiner said.
Within two feet of where the examiner said.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exactly where the examiner told you.
questions.explanation: Park your vehicle in the exact spot the examiner describes. If you do not finish an exercise exactly as instructed, you can lose points and may fail the basic control skills test.

questions.question: During a steering box inspection, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Check that the steering box is firmly attached.
Check that the steering box does not leak.
Look for missing bolts in the steering box.
Assume all cotter keys are present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume all cotter keys are present.
questions.explanation: Before a trip, check that the steering box is firmly attached. Look for missing nuts, bolts, and cotter keys. Check for power steering fluid leaks and damage to hoses.

questions.question: Which person should a driver NOT worry about?

options.text: A driver talking to a passenger
A child on the side of the road
A construction worker on the side of the road
A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus

questions.correctAnswerText: A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus
questions.explanation: Be careful when driving near people who are not paying attention to the road. Watch out for road workers, drivers talking with passengers, and children near the road.

questions.question: When you start a vehicle, warning lights and buzzers should:

options.text: Turn off within a few seconds.
Stay on until you turn them off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off within a few seconds.
questions.explanation: After starting the engine, warning lights and buzzers for oil, coolant, charging circuits, and the Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) should turn off right away.

questions.question: If you hear an unusual noise or feel something odd while driving, you should:

options.text: Hope the vehicle lasts until someone else drives it.
Stop and inspect the vehicle to find the problem.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and inspect the vehicle to find the problem.
questions.explanation: If you see, hear, smell, or feel anything unusual while driving, stop and check what is wrong.

questions.question: If another driver is tailgating you, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Avoid quick changes in speed or direction.
Increase the distance between you and the car ahead.
Avoid using tricks to help them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up.
questions.explanation: If being tailgated, increase your following distance, avoid quick moves, and do not use tricks like flashing lights to help them pass. Speeding up will only make the danger worse.

questions.question: You should always be able to stop within:

options.text: The distance you can see ahead.
One minute after hitting the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The distance you can see ahead.
questions.explanation: Make sure your vehicle can stop within the area of road you can see. Slow down when you cannot see far ahead.

questions.question: A cardboard box on the road:

options.text: May contain a heavy object that could damage your vehicle.
Should be avoided by driving off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: May contain a heavy object that could damage your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Any object on the road is dangerous. A cardboard box or paper sack might contain something hard or heavy that could seriously damage your vehicle.

questions.question: If you are not sure your vehicle will fit safely under a bridge, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: If you are not sure you have enough room under a bridge or overhead object, slow down and find a different route if possible.

questions.question: Which is NOT a sign of fatigue?
questions.correctAnswerText: Ability to focus
questions.explanation: Driving while tired is dangerous. Signs of fatigue include trouble focusing, repeated yawning or eye rubbing, daydreaming, and drifting out of your lane.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with air brakes, check that spring brakes activate automatically when:
questions.correctAnswerText: Air pressure drops below 45 psi.
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with air brakes, check that spring brakes turn on automatically when air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi. Block the wheels and release air from the brake system by pressing and releasing the brake pedal. When pressure gets too low, the parking brake valve should pop out and spring brakes should activate.

questions.question: If you are convicted of a traffic violation, you must tell your employer within how long?
questions.correctAnswerText: Within 30 days
questions.explanation: You must notify your employer within 30 days of a traffic conviction. This rule does not apply to parking violations.

questions.question: Dry bulk tanks need special care because:

options.text: They have low centers of gravity.
They have high centers of gravity.

questions.correctAnswerText: They have high centers of gravity.
questions.explanation: Dry bulk tanks have high centers of gravity. Their loads can also shift during driving. Be extra careful when turning or taking curves.

questions.question: When you approach an active railroad crossing, remember:

options.text: You will hear any train coming.
You may not hear a train coming.
You will hear two short horn blasts.
There will always be flashing lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not hear a train coming.
questions.explanation: Do not assume you will hear an approaching train. Trains may not sound their horns in some areas. Your vehicle's noise may block the sound. Do not rely on lights or other signals alone.

questions.question: What affects stopping distance?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance is affected by speed. The faster you drive, the longer it takes to stop.

questions.question: When checking tires during a vehicle inspection, you should:

options.text: Make sure the insides are more worn than the outsides.
Make sure the outsides are more worn than the insides.
Make sure the middles are more worn than the outsides.
Make sure the tires have even wear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the tires have even wear.
questions.explanation: Check that tire treads are worn evenly across the tire.

questions.question: Rough acceleration is:

options.text: Bad because it can damage the vehicle.
Bad because it confuses other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bad because it can damage the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Accelerate smoothly and slowly. Rough acceleration can harm your vehicle's engine and parts.

questions.question: When backing up with a trailer, you should:

options.text: Turn the steering wheel in the direction you want to go.
Turn the steering wheel opposite to the direction you want to go.
Turn the wheel as far as it will go.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the steering wheel opposite to the direction you want to go.
questions.explanation: With a trailer, turn the wheel the opposite way from where you want the trailer to go. Once the trailer starts turning, turn the wheel the other way to follow it.

questions.question: For a double combination vehicle, the maximum air leak during a static leakage test is:
questions.correctAnswerText: 3 psi in one minute.
questions.explanation: A double combination vehicle should lose no more than 3 psi of air pressure in one minute. If it leaks faster, the brakes need repair and the vehicle should not be driven.

questions.question: Do not use the parking brake if:

options.text: There is snow on the ground.
There is water on the ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes are very hot.
questions.explanation: Do not use the parking brake when brakes are hot from steep downhill driving or when brakes are wet and it is freezing. Hot brakes can be damaged. Wet brakes in freezing weather can freeze up and lock the wheels.

questions.question: A commercial motor vehicle must:

options.text: Have a fire extinguisher only if carrying hazardous materials.
Have a fire extinguisher only when traveling through remote areas.
Have a fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment.
questions.explanation: All commercial motor vehicles must have emergency equipment. This includes a fire extinguisher, spare fuses, and reflective warning triangles or flares.
